item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The HSC and its principals committee are directed to coordinate policy and are assigned internal composition, attendance, and staffing arrangements; these administrative effects operate within the executive branch rather than changing legal rights.","evidence":"The HSC Principals Committee (HSC/ PC) shall be the senior interagency forum under the HSC for homeland security issues."},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The Assistant to the President controls when this internal committee meets and sets its agenda, with no substantive legal consequence specified.","evidence":"The Assistant to the President for Homeland Security shall determine the agenda, in consultation with the regular attendees,"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The responsible official must arrange preparation of internal meeting materials; the consequence is administrative and occurs as the meetings are prepared.","evidence":"shall ensure that all necessary papers are prepared."},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"Presidential assistants and the Deputies Committee receive coordination, review, membership, staffing, and meeting responsibilities within the executive branch, without any dictated legal outcome for regulated parties.","evidence":"The HSC/DC shall serve as the senior sub-Cabinet interagency forum for consideration of policy issues affecting homeland security."},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The committee chairman is assigned authority to set meeting agendas after internal consultation; no legal consequence outside committee management occurs.","evidence":"the Chairman shall determine the agenda, in consultation with the regular members,"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The chairman must ensure preparation of internal committee papers, an administrative task whose effect arises during meeting preparation.","evidence":"shall ensure that necessary papers are prepared."},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"The policy coordination committees must coordinate agencies' development and implementation of policy, but the segment does not dictate any particular legally consequential policy result.","evidence":"shall coordinate the development and implementation of homeland security policies"},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"The committees are assigned intergovernmental and day-to-day policy-coordination roles, constituting internal management rather than a change in legal rights or duties.","evidence":"shall coordinate those policies with State and local government."},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"The committees must provide analysis, support responses to presidential decisions, and maintain specified agency representation; these are executive deliberation and organization functions.","evidence":"They shall provide policy analysis for consideration by the more senior committees of the HSC system"},{"segment_id":"10","code":1,"rationale":"The directive immediately establishes and staffs internal policy committees, an executive organizational change expressly covered by internal-management Code 1 rather than a substantive legal consequence.","evidence":"Eleven HSC/PCCs are hereby established for the following functional areas"},{"segment_id":"11","code":1,"rationale":"Executive officials receive administrative duties and discretionary authority over meeting attendance, additional committees, and working groups; all consequences concern internal organization and operation.","evidence":"may establish subordinate working groups to assist the PCC in the performance of its duties."}]}
